phrases.text: Bond Question 3 is about borrowing for higher education.
A general obligation bond is money the state borrows and repays with interest, generally over up to eleven years.
Today, the bonds cannot be issued without voter approval.
Bond Question 3 would allow up to $352,225,379 for improvements and acquisitions in higher education, special schools and tribal schools.
The Legislative Finance Committee puts all three bond questions at about 0.136 percent of the net taxable value of property.
The State Board of Finance will set the tax rate and yearly cost to property owners after the election.
New Mexico's voter guide includes no official argument for the bond question.
New Mexico's voter guide includes no official argument against the bond question.
A vote for authorizes the bonds, and the property tax to repay them.
A vote against means the bonds would not be issued.
